subject: Cloud Computing
title: The Carbon Cost of Cloud
description: Learn The Carbon Cost of Cloud in one minute.

hook.text: Data centers consume 1-2% of global electricity. As AI and cloud grow, that number is climbing fast.

buildup.text: A single data center can use as much electricity as a small city. Cooling alone accounts for 40% of energy consumption.

discovery.text: Cloud providers are investing billions in renewable energy: solar farms, wind power, and even nuclear partnerships.

twist.text: Moving to the cloud is often greener than on-premises. Shared infrastructure runs at higher utilization — less waste.

climax.text: AWS, Google, and Microsoft have pledged carbon neutrality. But growing demand may outpace renewable investments.

punchline.text: Cloud is greener than on-premises. But growing demand challenges that edge.

quiz.question: Why is moving to the cloud often greener than on-premises?
options: Shared cloud infrastructure runs at higher utilization, wasting less energy per workload
Cloud data centers don't use any electricity
On-premises servers are always powered by fossil fuels

details.summary: Cloud computing's carbon footprint comes from electricity generation, embodied emissions in hardware manufacturing, and cooling systems. While cloud is more efficient than on-premises computing, the total scale of cloud consumption means its absolute carbon emissions are substantial and growing.
details.whyItMatters: As cloud usage grows, its environmental impact becomes a corporate responsibility concern. Understanding carbon costs helps organizations make sustainable technology choices.
takeaways: Cloud data centers consume over 1% of global electricity
Embodied emissions from hardware manufacturing are significant
Carbon intensity varies dramatically by region and power source

faq.question: How much carbon does cloud computing produce?
faq.answer: Cloud data centers produce an estimated 2 to 3 percent of global carbon emissions, comparable to the aviation industry. Individual workload carbon depends on the region's power mix: a workload in a coal-powered region produces 10 to 50 times more carbon than one powered by renewables.

faq.question: How can organizations reduce cloud carbon?
faq.answer: Choose regions powered by renewables. Right-size resources to eliminate waste. Use ARM-based instances which are more power-efficient. Schedule batch workloads for times when the grid is cleanest. Use carbon tracking tools provided by cloud providers to measure and reduce emissions.
